top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) remains my first choice on literary grounds. Her voice is recognisable within a few lines. She treats genre boundaries as material and renews lyric, verse narrative, elegy and the essay from book to book. Eros the Bittersweet, Plainwater, Autobiography of Red, The Beauty of the Husband and Nox are different kinds of book, which I read as development and not repetition of one gesture. In Autobiography of Red and Nox the formal invention carries the feeling, and that is why I read the work as meeting the will's 'ideal direction' as depth and seriousness of imaginative purpose. The citation should rest on the original poetry, verse narrative and essays, with translation named only as part of the same practice, and it should not claim that the post-2010 books equal the core. Cărtărescu (P002) is a close second. His single obsessive cosmology runs from the poetry through the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid and has great scale and a distinctive voice. The gap between the two is small, and I rank him above no award because his claim is serious. My ordering partly reflects that I can judge Carson's English directly and cannot judge Romanian sentence texture, so I am unevenly informed. I do not count the four-member support for Carson as a literary reason. I have not independently verified any source or re-read the later Carson books. Whether they keep the level of the core, and how much of her design-dependent effect survives ordinary editions and translation, remain open. If close readers found the later work to be mainly erudite play, or showed the late Cărtărescu volumes to develop the project, my order would change. No award (P000) is last because both proposed writers meet the common criteria of voice, formal achievement and sustained depth well enough to justify an award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my shared first name with Anne Carson is coincidental, and my own novels and recorded statements are context only and are not evidence of preference
